'''Kristaps Porziņģis''' ({{IPA|lv|ˈkris.taps ˈpuɔr.ziɲ.ɟis}}; born 2 August 1995) is a Latvian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''the Unicorn'''" for his ability to make plays and shoot three-pointers as a [[Center (basketball)|center]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/kristaps-porzingis-nickname-kevin-durant-celtics-unicorn/4716028c4b61a38230e75fe3 |title=What is Kristaps Porzingis' nickname? How Kevin Durant coined Celtics star center's 'Unicorn' moniker |publisher=Sporting News |date=9 June 2024 }}</ref> Porziņģis is listed at {{height|ft=7|in=2}}{{efn|Porziņģis was measured to be {{height|ft=7|in=2+3/4}} barefoot prior to the 2019–20 season.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | last=Townsend |first=Brad | url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2019/09/30/mavericks-tales-of-the-tape-j-j-barea-no-longer-a-6-footer-porzingis-comes-in-just-shorter-than-boban/ | title=Mavericks tales of the tape: J.J. Barea no longer a 6-footer; Porzingis comes in just shorter than Boban | publisher=The Dallas Morning News | date=30 September 2019 }}</ref>}} and plays as a [[power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]].

Born in [[Liepāja]], Porziņģis began his professional career with [[CB Sevilla|Sevilla]] in 2012. Porziņģis quickly rose through the team's youth ranks and became the figurehead of the senior team by 2013. He subsequently won the [[EuroCup Basketball Rising Star]] award in 2015, where, at age 19, Porziņģis became the youngest-ever recipient of the award. The following summer, he declared for the [[NBA draft]] and was selected fourth overall by the [[New York Knicks]].

In New York, Porziņģis was seen as one of the Knicks' potential cornerstones, and he was selected as an [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] in [[2018 NBA All-Star Game|2018]]. However, disagreements with the front office led Porziņģis to be traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2019. In Dallas, he was plagued by injuries and inconsistent play and was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2022. In Washington, Porziņģis bounced back, but was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in 2023 as part of the Wizards' front office's desire to rebuild.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Greenberg |first=Neil |date=2023-06-26 |title=Analysis {{!}} The Wizards are taking a smart approach, but don't expect a quick fix |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2023/06/23/how-long-will-wizards-rebuild-take/ |access-date=2023-08-08 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> He won an NBA championship with the Celtics in 2024 before being traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-kristaps-porzingis|title=Atlanta Hawks acquire Kristaps Porziņģis|publisher=NBA.com|date=7 July 2025}}</ref>
{{toclimit|3}}

==Early career==
Porziņģis followed in his parents' footsteps and started playing basketball at age six.<ref name= eurocup/> Once he turned 12, his older brother, [[Jānis Porziņģis|Jānis]], who played professionally in Europe, took Porziņģis to offseason training sessions.<ref>{{cite news|last=Begley|first=Ian|title=Big brothers are watching Kristaps Porzingis and it's paying off|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/14373136|access-date=15 December 2015|publisher=ESPN|date=15 December 2015|archive-date=16 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151216014952/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/14373136/nba-kristaps-porzingis-owes-success-basketball-life-family|url-status=live}}</ref> He played in youth competitions with [[BK Liepājas Lauvas]], the most famous club based in his hometown of [[Liepāja]], until age 15. An agent from Latvia sent video of Porziņģis around this time to teams in Spain and Italy.<ref name= eurocup/> In 2010, [[CB Sevilla|Baloncesto Sevilla]], a club that had a professional team competing in the [[Liga ACB]] in Spain, called Porziņģis for a tryout in an attempt to recruit foreign talent to its junior squads. He stood {{Height|ft=6|in=8}} and weighed {{cvt|157|lb}} at this time.<ref name= eurocup>{{cite web| url= http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/features/player-spotlight/i/141583|title=Kristaps Porzingis, Baloncesto Seville |work= Eurocupbasketball.com|access-date=14 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623005146/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/features/player-spotlight/i/141583|archive-date=23 June 2018}}</ref><ref name= draftexpress>{{cite web|title=Kristaps Porzingis|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Kristaps-Porzingis-7119/|website=Draft Express|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=19 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150619001133/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/kristaps-porzingis-7119|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis recalled the moment and said, "I came here with my brother for two or three days, but it was really hot and I couldn't play at my best because of that. Still, I received a contract in summer 2010 and I signed it."<ref name=eurocup/> Inmaculada Avivar, a nutritionist for Sevilla, diagnosed that Porziņģis was suffering from [[anemia]], meaning that he had fewer [[red blood cell]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Anemia|url=http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/anemia|website=Merriam-Webster: Dictionary and Thesaurus|access-date=7 July 2014|archive-date=26 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826022138/http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/anemia|url-status=live}}</ref> This caused Porziņģis to feel fatigue, shortness of breath, and inability to exercise. However, he gradually overcame the condition and began seeing improvement in his game.<ref name=eurocup/> In addition to medical problems, Porziņģis had trouble picking up the [[Spanish language|language]] in [[Seville]], making him reluctant to return there after his first tryout. In his first season playing for the junior squad, Porziņģis struggled to communicate with the coaching staff and his teammates and was often tired due to his health.<ref name=eurocup/>

Porziņģis debuted for the youth squad on 4 January 2012 against its counterpart from [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]], adding 12 points and 10 rebounds. The opposing side was led by Alexander Zhigulin, who went on to enter the [[2015 NBA draft]] and withdraw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexandr Zhigulin Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Alexandr-Zhigulin/Summary/25104|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620225326/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Alexandr-Zhigulin/Summary/25104|url-status=live}}</ref> However, Sevilla was defeated, 56–75.<ref>{{cite web|title=FC Barcelona Regal Junior Team 75, Cajasol Seville Junior Team 56|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-01-04/FC-Barcelona-Regal-Junior-Team-at-Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team/87361|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620224847/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-01-04/FC-Barcelona-Regal-Junior-Team-at-Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team/87361|url-status=live}}</ref> This game was part of the Ciutat de L'Hospitalet tournament, which led up to the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Nike International Junior Tournament]] (NIJT).<ref name=eurocup/> The following day, Porziņģis scored a personal best of 16 points on the [[OKK Spars Sarajevo|Spars Sarajevo]] youth squad, helping Sevilla beat their opponents by a margin of eight points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cajasol Seville Junior Team 80, KK Spars Junior Team 72|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-01-05/Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team-at-KK-Spars-Junior-Team/87369|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620231725/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-01-05/Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team-at-KK-Spars-Junior-Team/87369|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis said, "I knew it was a prestigious tournament and that I had to do well. I think I could have done much better, but I wasn't physically 100 percent. I have seen videos and could have been much more aggressive. But I wish I could have played better."<ref name=eurocup/> He finished the tournament averaging 9.2 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.6 blocks.<ref name=eurocup/>

Porziņģis represented the Sevilla junior team again at the same tournament in early 2013. Against [[KK Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] on 4 January, he recorded 15 points and six rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Union Olimpija Junior Team 70, Cajasol Seville Junior Team 78|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-04/Union-Olimpija-Junior-Team-at-Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team/120276|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620230627/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-04/Union-Olimpija-Junior-Team-at-Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team/120276|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later in the team's tournament finale vs [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid]]'s youth squad, Porziņģis scored 24 points and grabbed 11 rebounds. He also made five three-pointers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cajasol Seville Junior Team 66, Real Madrid Junior Team 72|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-06/Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team-at-Real-Madrid-Junior-Team/120286|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620231605/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-06/Cajasol-Seville-Junior-Team-at-Real-Madrid-Junior-Team/120286|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis proved to be more effective in his second year, averaging 16.6 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.6 blocks and shooting .481 on three-pointers.<ref name="eurocup"/> This was his final stint in the youth categories of Sevilla.

==Professional career==
===Sevilla (2012–2015)===
====2012–13: Rookie season====
Entering the [[2012–13 ACB season]], Sevilla had hired [[Aíto García Reneses]], who previously worked with the likes of [[Pau Gasol]], [[Juan Carlos Navarro (basketball)|Juan Carlos Navarro]], [[Ricky Rubio]] and [[Rudy Fernández (basketball)|Rudy Fernández]].<ref name=eurocup/> On 29 September 2012, Porziņģis got the opportunity to make an appearance with the club's first team, but was allowed to play for only a minute. Sevilla took a tremendous loss to [[CB Murcia]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Universidad Católica De Murcia CB 93, Baloncesto Sevilla 77|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-09-29/Universidad-Catolica-De-Murcia-CB-at-Baloncesto-Sevilla/103535|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620230026/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2012-09-29/Universidad-Catolica-De-Murcia-CB-at-Baloncesto-Sevilla/103535|url-status=live}}</ref> Following a return to the youth categories of the club at the Torneig de Bàsquet Junior Ciutat de L'Hospitalet, Porziņģis went back to competing for the senior squad. On 16 January 2013, he logged only four minutes against [[BC Spartak Saint Petersburg|Spartak Saint Petersburg]] in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], scoring no points, but contributing a rebound and an assist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Baloncesto Sevilla 59, Spartak Saint Petersburg 78|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-16/Baloncesto-Sevilla-at-Spartak-Saint-Petersburg/119941|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=20 June 2015|archive-date=20 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150620231602/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-01-16/Baloncesto-Sevilla-at-Spartak-Saint-Petersburg/119941|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis scored his first basket for the senior team on 20 February, in a rematch with Spartak. Porziņģis said, "I was very nervous at the beginning: I wanted to do well and not pick up turnovers. At the same time, I got a lot of confidence with players of my same age. That allowed me to play better with the first team and practice with more confidence."<ref name=eurocup/> On 4 May, Porziņģis posted a season-high seven points with the senior team, hitting two of three shots vs [[Bilbao Basket]] in [[Liga ACB|ACB]] competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bilbao Basket 81, Baloncesto Sevilla 60|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-05-04/Bilbao-Basket-at-Baloncesto-Sevilla/103817|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=22 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622203215/http://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2013-05-04/Bilbao-Basket-at-Baloncesto-Sevilla/103817|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2013–14: Second season and NBA consideration====
Porziņģis opened his second season on Sevilla's main squad strong in his third game against the [[EuroLeague]] team [[Saski Baskonia|Laboral Kutxa]], leading them to a 20-point ACB victory on 2 November 2013.<ref name=eurocup/> He notched 12 points, six rebounds and four blocks.<ref name=second>{{cite web|title=2013–2014 International Games|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kristaps-Porzingis/GameLogs/32861/International/2014|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=22 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622203548/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kristaps-Porzingis/GameLogs/32861/International/2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis broke his scoring record once more against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] on 30 November 2013, nearly leading his team to a victory.<ref name=eurocup/><ref name=second/> Against the very same team on 6 April 2014, Porziņģis scored a career-high 20 points, nailing two three-pointers.<ref name=second/> Despite his team losing, Porziņģis began to trend on social media due to his performance. Porziņģis said, "It was a very good game for me on offense. I didn't get any rebounds in that game. I had a good shooting night, but could have helped more on defense. Still, fans in Madrid gave me a nice ovation when I fouled out and I liked that a lot."<ref name="eurocup"/> On 25 May, he got the chance to face his idol [[Justin Doellman]] of Barcelona, whom he called the "best power forward in Spanish basketball". Porziņģis scored 14 points against Doellman's team.<ref name=eurocup/><ref name="second"/> In May 2014, Porziņģis was selected in the [[ACB Best Young Player Award|ACB All-Young Players Team]] of the [[2013–14 ACB season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=103864|title=2013–14 ACB All-Young players Team|date=20 May 2014|publisher=ACB.com|language=es|access-date=2 June 2014|archive-date=26 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726174957/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=103864}}</ref>

In April, Porziņģis declared himself eligible for the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diena.lv/sports/basketbols/porzingis-tomer-pieteicies-nba-draftam-14053842|title=Porziņģis tomēr pieteicies NBA draftam|date=28 April 2014|publisher=Diena.lv|language=lv|access-date=29 April 2014|archive-date=29 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429204819/http://www.diena.lv/sports/basketbols/porzingis-tomer-pieteicies-nba-draftam-14053842|url-status=live}}</ref> Before and after he made the decision, Porziņģis drew interest from [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) teams such as the [[Orlando Magic]], who held the 12th overall pick, and traveled to Europe to scout him. The [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] reportedly were certainly going to select Porziņģis with the 21st pick in the case that he remained. Porziņģis was considered an unfinished product and a top-15 draft pick. According to DraftExpress.com, he was the fourth-youngest prospect in their top-100 rankings.<ref name=draftexpress/><ref>{{cite web|last=Herbert|first=James|title=NBA Draft 2014: Latvian prospect Kristaps Porzingis to enter draft|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/4/28/5660788/kristaps-porzingis-nba-draft|website=SB Nation|date=28 April 2014|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=26 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626123442/http://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/4/28/5660788/kristaps-porzingis-nba-draft|url-status=live}}</ref> However, Porziņģis withdrew his name shortly before the draft. Porziņģis's [[sports agent|agent]] Andy Miller released the information to [[ESPN]], saying that his client did not feel prepared to become a part of the NBA and wanted to develop his skills until the [[2015 NBA draft|2015 draft]]. One of the league's general managers commented on Porziņģis, "He's very talented. He wasn't ready, but we would've seriously considered drafting him anyway. If he continues to develop his game, get more minutes and his body develops, I think he could be a top-five pick in 2015. He has that kind of talent."<ref>{{cite web|last=Ford|first=Chad|title=Kristaps Porzingis pulls out of draft|date=16 June 2014|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/11090062|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=22 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622220338/http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/11090062/2014-nba-draft-kristaps-porzingis-latvia-pulls-draft|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2014–15: EuroCup Rising Star====
Prior to the [[2014–15 ACB season]], head coach Aíto García Reneses parted ways with Sevilla.<ref>{{cite web|title=Coach Aito Reneses leaves Cajasol Sevilla|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/126153/coach-aito-reneses-leaves-cajasol-sevilla.html|website=Sportando.com|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623002242/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/126153/coach-aito-reneses-leaves-cajasol-sevilla.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 4 October 2014, against [[CB 1939 Canarias]], Porziņģis made his season debut in the Liga ACB, scoring three points in the game. Porziņģis made his first appearance at the [[2014–15 Eurocup Basketball|2014–15 EuroCup]] on 15 October against [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]] and scored two points. However, Porziņģis had a strong EuroCup performance against [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma]] in the weeks that followed, in which he contributed 18 points, seven rebounds, four assists, four steals and two blocks. Porziņģis recorded a double-double in mid-November in a win over [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]], adding 11 points and 11 rebounds. On 11 February 2015, he scored a season-high 19 points against the EuroCup's [[Turów Zgorzelec]]. Porziņģis tied this record on 18 April, vs. [[Bàsquet Manresa]] in the ACB.<ref>{{cite web|title=2014–2015 International Games|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kristaps-Porzingis/GameLogs/32861|website=[[RealGM]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623002029/http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kristaps-Porzingis/GameLogs/32861|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days earlier, Porziņģis was named the winner of the [[EuroCup Basketball Rising Star|EuroCup Rising Star]] Award of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/5vvspvb5hnnlj9ye|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417033307/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/5vvspvb5hnnlj9ye|archive-date=17 April 2015|title=2014–15 Eurocup Rising Star Trophy winner: Kristaps Porzingis, Baloncesto Seville|publisher=Eurocupbasketball.com|access-date=14 April 2015}}</ref> A month later, he repeated in the ACB All-Young Players Team, after avoiding the [[promotion and relegation|relegation]] with Baloncesto Sevilla.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=113351 Mejor Quinteto Joven de la Liga Endesa 2014–15] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150521193736/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=113351 |date=21 May 2015 }}; ACB.com, 19 May 2015</ref>

===New York Knicks (2015–2019)===
[[File:Kristaps Porzingis.jpg|thumb|left|Porziņģis during [[2015 NBA Summer League]]]]
On 16 April 2015, Porziņģis entered the [[2015 NBA draft]], according to a report from agent Andy Miller.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ford |first=Chad |date=16 April 2015 |title=Latvian power forward Kristaps Porzingis to enter draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2015/story/_/id/12698126 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421055416/http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2015/story/_/id/12698126/latvian-power-forward-kristaps-porzingis-declare-nba-draft |archive-date=21 April 2015 |access-date=22 May 2015 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> After gaining a season more of experience, Porziņģis became known as a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] pick and a potential top-five selection. He drew interest from teams such as the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], who had the No. 2 pick and had several personnel that had seen Porziņģis play in Spain.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ding|first=Kevin|title=Mystery Man Kristaps Porzingis Tempts Many in NBA Draft, but Will Any Team Bite?|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2503065-mystery-man-kristaps-porzingis-tempts-many-in-nba-draft-but-will-any-team-bite|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623104855/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2503065-mystery-man-kristaps-porzingis-tempts-many-in-nba-draft-but-will-any-team-bite|url-status=live}}</ref> Porziņģis was compared with players such as [[Pau Gasol]] and [[Dirk Nowitzki]], but also [[Darko Miličić]], a former lottery selection widely considered a [[draft bust]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Murphy|first=David|title=Why Kristaps Porzingis Could Be the Shocker of the 2015 NBA Draft Class|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2500096-why-kristaps-porzingis-could-be-the-shocker-of-the-2015-nba-draft-class|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623044632/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2500096-why-kristaps-porzingis-could-be-the-shocker-of-the-2015-nba-draft-class|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Adrian Wojnarowski]] of [[Yahoo! Sports]] wrote, "Porziņģis has an innate awareness about the way the American public sees a young, long European teenager. He comes to the NBA with the full understanding that popular basketball culture declares him guilty until proven innocent of the basketball crimes of [[Darko Miličić]] and [[Nikoloz Tskitishvili]] and [[Andrea Bargnani]]. ====2020–21: Playoff fallout====
[[File:Kristaps Porzingis floater (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Porziņģis in 2020]]
Porziņģis had surgery on his torn lateral meniscus on 9 October 2020.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Dallas Mavericks' Kristaps Porziņģis has knee surgery to repair lateral meniscus tear | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30080038|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|author-link=Tim MacMahon | date = 9 October 2020 | access-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211023223937/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30080038/dallas-mavericks-kristaps-porzingis-knee-surgery-repair-lateral-meniscus-tear | url-status = live }}</ref> Porziņģis went on to miss the first nine games of the [[2020-21 NBA season]] recovering from surgery. He made his season debut on 13 January 2021, against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], where he scored 16 points while held to a 21-minute restriction.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Kristaps Porziņģis scores 16 in season debut for Mavs | website = [[NBA.com]] | url = https://www.nba.com/news/kristaps-porzingis-set-to-return-from-injury-vs-hornets | date = 13 January 2021 | access-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211023223935/https://www.nba.com/news/kristaps-porzingis-set-to-return-from-injury-vs-hornets | url-status = live }}</ref> As a precautionary measure, Porziņģis did not play in the majority of back-to-back games during the regular season. On 12 February, he scored a season-high 36 points with a career-high eight made three pointers in a 143–130 victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web | title = New Orleans Pelicans at Dallas Mavericks Box Score, February 12, 2021 | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202103260DAL.html | date = 12 February 2021 | access-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211023223938/https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202103260DAL.html | url-status = live }}</ref> On 26 March, Porziņģis tied a career high by grabbing 18 rebounds in a 109–94 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web | title = Indiana Pacers at Dallas Mavericks Box Score, March 26, 2021 | url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202103260DAL.html | date = 26 March 2021 | access-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-date = 23 October 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211023223938/https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202103260DAL.html | url-status = live }}</ref> Dallas improved on their previous season record and finished the 2020–21 season with a 42–30 record. The Mavericks clinched the Southwest division for the first time since the [[2009–10 Dallas Mavericks season|2009–10 season]] following a 110–90 victory over the [[2020-21 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] on 7 May.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mavs beat the Cavs |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavsclinchdivision/ |website=The Official Home of the Dallas Mavericks |access-date=6 July 2021 |date=8 May 2021 |archive-date=12 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512152206/https://www.mavs.com/mavsclinchdivision/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Porziņģis finished the season averaging 20.1 points per game and 8.9 rebounds per game. The 2020–21 season proved to be his most efficient season of his career thus far, posting career highs in eFG%, TS% and FG% statistics. Porziņģis became just the sixth player in franchise history to have multiple seasons averaging over 20 points per game, joining [[Mark Aguirre]], [[Rolando Blackman]], [[Luka Dončić]], [[Michael Finley]] and [[Dirk Nowitzki]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Mavericks All-Time Points Leaders: Single Regular Season Per Game Average|url = https://www.landofbasketball.com/all_time_leaders/mavericks/points_pg_single_rs.htm|date = 23 October 2021|access-date = 23 October 2021|archive-date = 23 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211023223937/https://www.landofbasketball.com/all_time_leaders/mavericks/points_pg_single_rs.htm|url-status = live}}</ref>

However, Porziņģis' numbers dropped drastically during the first round of the playoffs, averaging 13.1 points per game and grabbing 5.4 rebounds per game. The Mavericks went on to lose in the first round to the [[2020-21 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] for the second consecutive season in seven games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clippers win Game 7, eliminate Mavericks despite Luka Doncic's 46 points |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2021-06-06/clippers-win-game-7-mavericks-luka-doncic-kawhi-leonard |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=6 July 2021 |date=6 June 2021 |archive-date=20 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620090345/https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2021-06-06/clippers-win-game-7-mavericks-luka-doncic-kawhi-leonard |url-status=live }}</ref> Following the series, Porziņģis was roundly mocked by fans for his subpar performance during the series, with many calling him "Pandemic P",<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://fansided.com/2021/06/06/nba-twitter-roasts-kristaps-porzingis-mavericks-clippers/|title = NBA Twitter roasts Kristaps Porzingis as new 'Pandemic P'|date = 6 June 2021|access-date = 28 October 2021|archive-date = 28 October 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211028011855/https://fansided.com/2021/06/06/nba-twitter-roasts-kristaps-porzingis-mavericks-clippers/|url-status = live}}</ref> a name originally used for mocking [[Paul George]] for his abysmal performance during the 2020 playoffs. Porziņģis was disgruntled with his role in the first round series against the Clippers, often being relegated to a decoy or three-point spacing threat. Rumors of Porziņģis wanting a trade in the offseason began to form, but nothing came of it. He began training for the upcoming season. In an Instagram post, Porziņģis vowed to come back stronger and more refined and that the Unicorn 2.0 was incoming.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thesportsrush.com/nba-news-yall-about-to-see-unicorn-2-0-kristaps-porzingis-vows-to-return-in-beastly-for-dallas-mavericks-next-year-after-lackluster-2020-21-season/|title="Y'all about to see Unicorn 2.0": Kristaps Porzingis vows to return in beastly form for Dallas Mavericks next year after lackluster 2020–21 season|date=7 November 2021|access-date=8 November 2021|archive-date=8 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108173105/https://thesportsrush.com/nba-news-yall-about-to-see-unicorn-2-0-kristaps-porzingis-vows-to-return-in-beastly-for-dallas-mavericks-next-year-after-lackluster-2020-21-season/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Porziņģis also missed the entirety of the Celtics' next two series against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and [[Indiana Pacers]], as the Celtics advanced to the [[2024 NBA Finals]] to face the [[2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], his former team. Porziņģis returned for Game 1 of the Finals on 6 June, coming off the bench and scoring 18 of his 20 points in the first half.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/kristaps-porzingis-progressing-return-2024-nba-finals-celtics-mavericks|title=Kristaps Porzingis suits up, plays big off bench in Celtics' Game 1 win over Mavericks|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=6 June 2024|access-date=8 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zillgitt |first=Jeff |title=Kristaps Porzingis' instant impact off bench in NBA Finals Game 1 exactly what Celtics needed |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2024/06/06/kristaps-porzingis-impacts-game-1-nba-finals-celtics-return/74008054007/ |access-date=2024-06-07 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> Three days later, in Game 2, Porziņģis developed a new injury with a "torn medial retinaculum, allowing dislocation of the posterior tibialis tendon" in his left leg that was considered completely unrelated to the previous calf injury he had dealt with for most of the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Maloney |first=Jack |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/kristaps-porzingis-rare-injury-explaining-medically-what-celtics-center-is-dealing-with-during-nba-finals/ |title=Kristaps Porzingis' 'rare' injury: Explaining medically what Celtics center is dealing with during NBA Finals |work=CBS Sports |date=12 June 2024 }}</ref> Despite missing the next two games, Porziņģis returned in Game 5 on 17 June, where he scored five points and helped the Celtics secure their record-setting 18th championship.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40373175 |title=Kristaps Porzingis (leg) returns as Celtics win title; surgery next |publisher=ESPN |date=17 June 2024 }}</ref>

On 27 June 2024, Porziņģis underwent surgery to repair his retinaculum injury with a recovery timetable being set at five to six months, ruling Porziņģis out for the beginning of the [[2024–25 NBA season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics' Kristaps Porzingis has surgery, to miss start of season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40444852|access-date=28 June 2024|website=[[ESPN]]|date=27 June 2024 |language=en|last=Bontemps|first=Tim}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2025–2026)===
On 24 June 2025, [[Shams Charania]] of ESPN reported that the Celtics, Atlanta Hawks and Brooklyn Nets agreed to a three-team trade that would send Porziņģis and a second-round pick to the Hawks, [[Georges Niang]] and a second-round pick to the Celtics, and [[Terance Mann]] and the 22nd pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]]—used to select [[Drake Powell]]—to the Nets. The trade was formally announced on 7 July,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-kristaps-porzingis|title=Atlanta Hawks acquire Kristaps Porziņģis|access-date=7 July 2025|publisher=NBA.com|date=7 July 2025}}</ref> due to the [[NBA salary cap#July moratorium|July moratorium]] that was in effect for the [[2025–26 NBA season]] until 6 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-acquire-kristaps-porzingis-3-team-trade|title=Hawks acquire Celtics center Kristaps Porziņģis in 3-team trade|access-date=30 June 2025|publisher=NBA.com|date=24 June 2025}}</ref> Porziņģis made 17 appearances (including 12 starts) for Atlanta, posting averages of 17.1 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kristaps Porzingis 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3102531/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=2026-07-03|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2025, Porziņģis was diagnosed with [[postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome]] (POTS),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thesicktimes.org/2025/10/25/nba-player-kristaps-porzingis-shares-pots-diagnosis |title=NBA player Kristaps Porziņģis shares POTS diagnosis |website=The Sick Times |date=October 25, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref> a neurological disease that can be triggered by viral infections, especially SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19 which causes this syndrome in about 1% of infected people.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yong |first1=Shin Jie |last2=Halim |first2=Alice |title=Pooled rates and demographics of POTS following SARS-CoV-2 infection versus COVID-19 vaccination: Systematic review and meta-analysis |journal=Autonomic Neuroscience: Basic and Clinical |volume=250 |article-number=103132 |year=2023 |doi=10.1016/j.autneu.2023.103132 |pmid=38000119 |url=https://www.autonomicneuroscience.com/article/S1566-0702(23)00061-9/fulltext |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2026–present)===
On 5 February 2026, Porziņģis was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for guard [[Buddy Hield]] and forward [[Jonathan Kuminga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-kristaps-porzingis-from-atlanta-hawks-20260205|title=Warriors Acquire Kristaps Porzingis From Atlanta Hawks|work=NBA.com|date=5 February 2026}}</ref> He made 15 appearances (including 11 starts) for Golden State, averaging 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
Porziņģis played with the [[Latvia men's national under-17 basketball team|Latvian youth team]] and was selected in the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] All-Tournament Team.

===Senior national team===
In 2017, Porziņģis played for [[Latvia men's national basketball team|Latvia]] at [[EuroBasket 2017]], where he averaged 23.6 points per game (ranked third), 5.9 rebounds per game (ranked 19th) and 1.9 blocks per game (ranked first).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Kristaps-Porzingis|title=Kristaps PORZINGIS|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=12 November 2017|archive-date=13 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171113021430/http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/Kristaps-Porzingis|url-status=live}}</ref> Latvia was eliminated in the quarterfinals by eventual champions [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenia]], losing 97–103. Against Slovenia, Porziņģis scored a tournament-high 34 points despite playing in foul trouble throughout the game. He scored 16 of his 34 points in the final period to help Latvia cut Slovenia's 13-point lead to two with two minutes remaining.

After a five-year absence, in August 2022, Porziņģis returned to play for the national team in the August window of the second round of the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe) – Qualifiers|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 European Qualifiers]]. In two games, he averaged 25.5 points per game, 14.0 rebounds per game and 3.0 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/european-qualifiers/player/Kristaps-Porzingis|title=Kristaps PORZINGIS|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=14 November 2022|archive-date=14 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114022719/https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/european-qualifiers/player/Kristaps-Porzingis|url-status=live}}</ref> In a 111–85 victory over [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]], Porziņģis scored 22 points, grabbed 14 rebounds and blocked six shots in just 22 minutes of playing. In Latvia's 87–80 victory over [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain]], he had 14 rebounds and scored 29 points on 75% shooting.

==Personal life==
[[File:Kristaps Porzingis in 2017 summer.png|thumb|175px|Porziņģis in 2017]]
Porziņģis was born to parents who had experience playing [[basketball]]. Tālis, his father, competed semi-professionally before becoming a [[bus driver]]. His mother, Ingrīda, was previously on [[Latvia women's national basketball team|Latvia women's youth national basketball team]].<ref name=aol/> His older brother, [[Jānis Porziņģis|Jānis]], also played professionally,<ref name=eurocup/> while his oldest brother, Mārtiņš, who is approximately 15 years older than his youngest sibling, was also an avid player.<ref name=aol>{{cite web|last=Weitzman|first=Yaron|title=NBA Draft Watch: The Kristaps Porzingis Experience|url=http://www.aol.com/article/2015/06/22/nba-draft-watch-the-kristaps-porzingis-experience/21199493/|website=[[AOL]]|access-date=23 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623185047/http://www.aol.com/article/2015/06/22/nba-draft-watch-the-kristaps-porzingis-experience/21199493/|url-status=live}}</ref> In a 2017 ''[[E:60]]'' documentary on Porziņģis' life, his parents revealed that they had another son, Toms, who was born four years before Kristaps and died at the age of 14 months. Through an interpreter, Ingrīda said about Toms' death, "It felt like a bulldozer had run over my life. We had two other children who we had to care for. We had to live on. After Kristaps was born, it was like he had to live for two lives."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://nypost.com/2017/06/25/the-quiet-porzingis-family-tragedy/ |title='Had to live for two lives': The tragedy that shaped Kristaps Porzingis |first=Marc |last=Berman |newspaper=[[New York Post]] |date=25 June 2017 |access-date=28 June 2017 |archive-date=28 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628011829/http://nypost.com/2017/06/25/the-quiet-porzingis-family-tragedy/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Jānis Porziņģis competed at the [[European professional club basketball system|European second tier]] [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] level, the same level in Europe that Kristaps later played at, in one game,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/players/?seasoncode=U2004&pcode=JTZ |title=PORZINGIS, JANIS SUPERFUND KAPFENBERG BORN: 13 JULY, 1982 NATIONALITY: LATVIA. |access-date=9 February 2023 |archive-date=11 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411223749/https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/players/?seasoncode=U2004&pcode=JTZ |url-status=live }}</ref> and played European professional club basketball in various national leagues, including the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=POR-JAN-82|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222115943/http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=POR-JAN-82|title=Janis Porzingis|#10 Naz. di Nascita: LAT Naz. Sportiva: LAT Città di Nascita: Liepaja Altezza: 201 cm Data di Nascita: 13/07/1982 Peso: 102 kg|archive-date=22 December 2015}}</ref> for more than 10 years. He is known to mentor his younger brother on and off the court and often called him after playing games for Cajasol Sevilla in Spain. Porziņģis talked about the relationship in an interview, "We'd break down the details. We watched the film together. He's always pushing me to work hard. We just spend a lot of time together and we just talk about basketball all the time..."<ref name=interview>{{cite web|last=Robbins|first=Josh|title=A Q-and-A with NBA Draft prospect Kristaps Porzingis|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-kristaps-porzingis-interview-20150622-story.html#page=1|website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=22 June 2015 |access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623025246/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-kristaps-porzingis-interview-20150622-story.html#page=1|url-status=live}}</ref> The elder Porziņģis helped him train in the summer and work out in the gym in preparation for international competition in 2012.<ref name=eurocup/>

Following two seasons in Spain and almost two years living in Seville, Porziņģis was able to speak Spanish far more fluently. He is thus fluent in three different languages, including English.<ref name=eurocup/> An NBA executive said, "He speaks great English and I don't see it being that difficult of a transition off the court."<ref>{{cite web|title=Scotto: Kristaps Porzingis Transcends the European Stereotype|url=http://www.sheridanhoops.com/2015/06/19/scotto-kristaps-porzingis-transcends-the-european-stereotype/|website=SheridanHoops.com|access-date=22 June 2015|archive-date=22 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622103637/http://www.sheridanhoops.com/2015/06/19/scotto-kristaps-porzingis-transcends-the-european-stereotype|url-status=live}}</ref> In October 2016, Porziņģis signed a shoe deal with [[Adidas]], the most lucrative deal for a European player. ===Rape allegation and possible extortion===
In March 2019, it was publicly revealed that a woman accused Porziņģis of raping her at the [[Sky (skyscraper)|Sky]] building in February 2018, hours after he tore his ACL. The woman reportedly told police she waited more than a year to come forward because she had discussed getting a $68,000 payout from Porziņģis to keep quiet. Porziņģis' attorney, Roland G. Riopelle, publicly denied the claim, and said he had previously referred the case to federal authorities due to the "accuser's extortionate demands."<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Porzingis accused of rape in New York|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26401287|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=30 March 2019|access-date=31 March 2019|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331050154/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26401287/report-porzingis-accused-rape-new-york|url-status=live|others=Contributed by Ian Begley, [[Tim MacMahon]] and Royce Young}}</ref>
